body:
Tracks priority 1 of `docs/release/POST_FREEZE_TEST_PLAN.md` §0.

**Current state (PROVISIONAL, `SUPPORT.md` §0):** CPU and CUDA local alignment differ with 5 x 5 patches. Relative RMSE CPU vs CUDA is 0.43–0.60 on EMPIAR-10216, 10474 Falcon 3 and 12963, and 0.0013–0.014 on the tutorial, 10361, 10164 and 10028 (#209, main `1db86902`). The #212 diagnosis attributes this to near-tied CCF peaks, amplified by patch acceptance and the polynomial fit. The CPU tie rule (#70) does not explain it. The near-tie mechanism is not yet confirmed per frame.

**Campaign:**
- S1.1: multi-movie sweep, configs L and 3 x 3, over all ten #186 families. Record incidence per family, converged patch counts and differing patch sets.
- S1.2: longevity on builds older than `116eb04a`, with a CPU-vs-CPU control.
- S1.3: CCF near-tie logging, top two peaks per backend, on the divergent patches.
- S1.4: downstream CTF/FSC/B-factor, CPU vs CUDA (#61, #73). After that the maintainer confirms or changes the D7 support class.

Thresholds and gates stay unchanged.

S1.1, S1.2 and S1.3 start on 2026-10-19. Evidence lands as docs-only PRs under `docs/post_rc0/s1/`.

comments.body:
**Current result.** The first complete S1.1 pass covers all ten families (16 distinct movies, 5×5 and 3×3). The 5×5 large-disagreement cases are 10216, Falcon 3, 10641 and 12963; the second 10641 movie reaches relative RMSE 0.808. The 10216 3×3 case is 0.196 despite all nine patches being accepted on both backends.

**Evidence.** Ready-for-review docs-only PR #243 records per-movie backend gates/metrics, patch rows/sets, hashes, argv, exits and UUID witnesses. S1.2 reproduces 0.434362/0.599858 on both selected movies at `2ff18e93`, `c499b1d3` and `6b6adf44`; all six CPU-versus-F controls are identical. This extends observed presence to 2026-09-27, without identifying an introduction commit. No timing or scientific-equivalence claim; gates/defaults unchanged.

**Next action.** Review #243 and extend the sparse families toward ≥10 distinct movies; the additional staged-movie pass is running separately. Keep S1.3/S1.4 as separate evidence.

**S1.3 result:** the near-tie mechanism is confirmed for all 9 S1-relevant patches in the five S1-positive cases (10216 3×3 and 5×5, 12963, Falcon 3 `…20-39-45`, 10641 `…004_0008`). The CCF map differences are consistent with rounding at every stage measured. Evidence: PR #250, `docs/post_rc0/s1/ccf_ties/README.md`.

- **Mechanism:** each S1-relevant patch first diverges where the backends pick different integer peaks in one frame.
  - In 7/9 patches the two candidates are ≤16 ulps apart on both maps; in 2/9 they are a ≤3-ulp tie on one map with a 36 or 68-ulp lead on the other.
  - 10216 3×3 has no acceptance flip: a 3/4-ulp adjacent-pixel near-tie in frame 1 (the reference frame) moves patch (2,1) by 1.13 px, and that patch accounts for most of the fit difference.
- **Rounding:** each backend's CCF map is within ≤9.4 ulps of float64. Global-alignment maps differ by ≤7 ulps at iteration 1, with no peak changes. Patch-input differences (median 0.29–0.64%) are the ≤0.038 px global-trajectory difference, propagated. CUDA's phase-shift error is ≤5.7e-7 and is not the cause.
- **Open:** the amplitude part of the patch-input difference (inferred crop effect), full-frame shift accuracy at large phases, and breadth beyond these five movies.

**Next:** review PR #250. S1.4 remains the test of whether the difference matters scientifically.

**S1.3b changes the S1.3 rounding conclusion.** The CPU/CUDA patch-input difference has a systematic CUDA-specific component. It is not all propagated rounding. Evidence: PR #250 commit `7fc9733f`, README Result (b).

- **Source:** a sub-pixel global shift makes the spectrum's Nyquist column non-Hermitian. cuFFT's C2R in the global inverse FFT turns that part into a per-row constant h(y) in the real frames; FFTW (CPU) discards it.
  - The full spectra agree to ≤1.93e-6, but the real frames differ by 7e-4–1e-2, all as h(y).
  - h(y) predicts the equal-trajectory patch-input difference to ≤5.8e-7.
- **The rest of the difference** is the shift/crop geometry of the ≤0.038 px global-trajectory difference. CPU given CUDA's trajectory reproduces the amplitude residual (3.60e-4 vs 3.68e-4; 5.85e-4 vs 6.02e-4).
- **Equal trajectories (CUDA given CPU's):**
  - 12963: all 5 S1-relevant flips persist, relative RMSE 0.4999.
  - 10216: the (1,4) near-tie recurs but the patch converges on CUDA, relative RMSE 0.021.
- **CCF computation and peak search** stay rounding-consistent.

**Next:** a diagnostic removal test of h(y) to establish it as the cause of the 12963 flips, and a check of whether h(y) reaches published products. Any fix is a product change and needs a maintainer decision.

**Current result.** S1.1 covers 114 distinct movies (24 tutorial; 10 per other family), both grids. Large-disagreement incidence at 5×5 / 3×3: 10216 **7/10 / 5/10**, Falcon 3 **4/10 / 1/10**, 10641 **5/10 / 0/10**, 12963 **7/10 / 3/10**; zero in the other families. This uses the descriptive relative-RMSE ≥0.1 screen, separate from unchanged backend gates. Non-convergence is associated with incidence but is neither necessary nor sufficient.

**Evidence.** Updated PR #243 (`4f57ac67`) retains per-movie metrics/patch sets and full provenance. **28/28** older CPU controls and **8/8** cross-venue controls pass. The sampled 10216 5×5 boundary is `ef7e4c0a` → `58fd513a` (0.018128 → 0.434362; both backend FAIL). 10216 3×3 and Falcon 3 5×5 are positive at earliest native probe `e875d5fe` (2026-09-24). One SCARF 40 GB CUDA OOM remains failed/UNRUN; all ten 10441 movies completed on 4GPUs 80 GB. Staged-controller resumption and missing SCARF launcher sentinels are recorded explicitly.

**Next action.** Review #243 alongside separate mechanism work #250; S1.4 remains outside this sweep. Exhaustive history, native `d01f512d` and full EMPIAR populations are unrun. No gate/default changes or timing/scientific-equivalence claims.

## Coordination handoff: validate the two fixes without making CPU bit-parity the objective

Reviewed the published heads and discussions: main `36913740`; Hermitian fix #254 at `8b55d5da`; census #255 at `23a320a6`; audit #256 now `f6257294`; active follow-ups #257, #258 and #259. This is a review/experiment plan for the existing agents, not a duplicate implementation, merge authorization or new native GPU result.

**Objective:** valid numerical operators, accurate known-motion recovery and acceptable downstream scientific results. CPU agreement remains a useful regression/diagnostic reference, not ground truth. Keep existing gates and recorded FAIL results unchanged while separately reporting correctness and scientific evidence.

### 1. Finish the portable #254 tests, keeping production scope narrow

The boundary projection and all five consumption sites look sound on source inspection. The branch is implemented but unmerged. Existing native evidence supports the contract repair; it is not S1 closure.

The revised tests should assert the actual Hermitian input invariant before every C2R and fail each selectively removed-callsite mutant without relying on cuFFT's undefined-input behavior. Additionally, the **positive FFTW oracle currently receives the same invalid spectrum**: construct an independently projected valid reference first. Retain the raw A100 leak as a characterized observation, not a universal negative-control requirement. Details: [#254 follow-up review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/254#pullrequestreview-5593330850).

CPU has the same representation hazard, but tested FFTW effectively drops the incompatible component. Explicit CPU-consumption projection and a scientifically specified Nyquist/crop-folding convention are separate follow-ups. Neither should silently broaden this CUDA PR.

### 2. Continue the already assigned #257 peak-fit experiment independently

Selective promotion is justified by a same-input arithmetic defect. Do not present it as the only possible remaining S1 source, guaranteed exact CPU matching, or measured negligible overhead. The reported maximum 0.13525164 px is **already after CCF scaling**; the ~0.045 px first-iteration observation is not a bound on a later census's accumulated global trajectory.

Use the actual production kernel, an independent same-sample oracle and a restoring mutant; specify threshold, scale and output-rounding semantics. Correcting cancellation can legitimately change a guard branch that formerly saw a rounded zero. Preserve tie/search/convergence policy for attribution; keep a new boundary-validity policy separate. Details: [#257 guidance](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/issues/257#issuecomment-6304604833).

### 3. Run a staged, source-pinned factorial comparison

Start from one common baseline and retain four arms: **baseline / Hermitian-only / peak-only / both**. On the selected mechanism cases add **global-only vs local-only peak promotion**. Fixed-trajectory/common-buffer controls separate direct reconstruction effects from estimator feedback. Avoid mixing unrelated admission, ingestion or model-policy changes into this first attribution experiment.

Capture first changed CCF samples, selected peaks, fitted candidates, reference-frame subtraction, per-iteration RMSD/stopping, final global trajectories, accepted patch sets, full-precision fitted coefficients, and both weighted/unweighted outputs. Record source/binary/input hashes, actual ingest/fallback routes, device UUID, toolchain and all native exits. Timing builds must not include diagnostic synchronisation overhead.

Then rerun all original 60 configurations, not only previous positives, plus the 10641 geometry and unaffected-family controls. Include newly worsened cases such as 10216-07/08 5×5 and 12963-08/09. The fixed operation is necessary even where a nonlinear near tie causes a new CPU-relative disagreement; that disagreement still must be reported and investigated.

For analysis, cluster the two grids by movie. The current 27→17 is a **configuration** count, while 'at least one grid positive' changes **19/30→15/30 movies**. The original configuration p-value reproduces, but it is not a 60-independent-movie result. I posted a movie-cluster sensitivity calculation and perturbation-control qualifications on [#255](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/255#pullrequestreview-5593341658). Keep continuous errors, all regressions and the descriptive screen separate from the strict backend gate and from scientific outcomes.

### 4. Investigate residuals selectively; prepare S1.4 now

If flat-peak sensitivity remains, zero only the CCF spectrum's DC term **before** inverse transformation in a diagnostic arm and compare against a higher-precision map reference. This distinguishes scalar curvature loss from information already lost in float map formation. Do not combine it with different B weights, tie rules or robust fitting in the same experiment.

Prepare the downstream protocol now, retain baseline products, then execute the expensive matched scientific comparisons on a frozen qualified candidate. Use known-truth synthetic shifts/deformations alongside CTF/FSC/B-factor comparisons with controlled particle selection, half sets and downstream settings. Exact CPU equality should not be a prerequisite for starting science; changing the candidate midway should trigger explicit versioned comparisons. Record native whole-movie cost as well as correctness.

### 5. Independent bugs and integration

#258 and #259 already exist; do not duplicate them. I added [gain representation/orientation test guidance](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/issues/258#issuecomment-6304642341) and [warp source-boundary/precision guidance](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/issues/259#issuecomment-6304645646). The generic `.gain` reader already dispatches TIFF on main; orientation and rewritten semantic meaning are the remaining issue. For warp incidence, inspect source-coordinate boundaries, which need not lie on the last output row/column.

The wrong coordinate domain in the distortion guard is a correctness defect; peak-edge policy and STAR round-trip precision also need explicit, separately tested compatibility decisions. Record inherited corrections under #216 rather than treating legacy output as automatically correct.

**Housekeeping status:** #256 has the census update and #243 has the 10216-01 shared-global-failure annotation. Keep the latter's raw inter-backend error: both algorithms failing does not mean their measured difference disappears. Any exclusion should be an explicit secondary analysis.

**Do not batch-approve the eight PRs in the earlier recommendation.** Two current heads still contain the already reviewed defects:
- **#244 (`88444f3e`)**: detached `Popen` remains outside cleanup protection, and repeated cancellation can interrupt TERM/reap. Source still matches the [existing cancellation review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/244#discussion_r4314688675). It is also currently conflicting with main. Fix/test spawn registration and repeated cancellation using harmless CPU children before treating the fault-test driver as ready.
- **#252 (`1fd0aea6`)**: `admitPatchRetry` still budgets only the downloaded spectrum, not the fresh alignment workspace subsequently allocated while the old workspace remains live. The [existing allocation-lifetime review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/252#discussion_r4315391298) still applies. Qualify a boundary where the spectrum fits but the complete simultaneous retry peak does not, or reuse/release the old workspace correctly.
- **#249 (`84872649`)** still reports a merge conflict. Preserve both acceptance-report entries when reconciling it, then rerun current-head CI. Positive source reviews of #245/#248/#249/#251 do not replace integration checks; #241/#242 have no review comments in the fetched threads. No blanket fresh approval is given here.

When combining #251/#252 and the numerical work, preserve all required-test registrations and fail-closed collection lists, reconcile documentation without dropping other evidence, and run the integrated Release suites. CUDA compile-only CI is not native execution. This plan leaves merges and output-policy sign-off with the maintainer.

## Revised conclusions and validation plan after #260/#261

**Maintainer direction:** focus on mathematical correctness, recovery of motion and preserved scientific information, rather than making CUDA reproduce whatever the legacy CPU implementation does. CPU comparisons remain useful diagnostics and compatibility records, not the scientific oracle. This updates the earlier [coordination plan](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/issues/238#issuecomment-6304699348); it is not blanket merge approval or permission to rewrite historical gates.

Reviewed snapshots: #254 `af2a5900`, #260 `d888ab11`, #261 `c89e74c2`, and follow-up issues #262–266. This review inspected source/tests and retained reports, with bounded host checks; it did not execute a new native GPU or downstream campaign.

### Conclusions that changed

1. **Hermitian repair remains justified by the input contract, independently of CPU agreement.** #254 now checks all five actual C2R inputs and kills each projection-removal mutant before cuFFT. Its production code is unchanged from the earlier reviewed implementation. The remaining output-oracle problem is that the positive inverse test still asks FFTW to invert the malformed spectrum. Use an independently valid reference. [Updated review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/254#pullrequestreview-5596691051).
2. **The peak-fit arithmetic defect is now fixed and demonstrated natively, but the principal-global-gap hypothesis was not supported.** In #261, #254-only versus #254+double fitting gives 17→19/60 fixed-reference screen positives, and median maximum global discrepancy in the other 58 cases is 0.038605→0.039105 px. Keep #260 for its accurate same-sample arithmetic, not as a proven scientific improvement or an S1 cure. [Focused review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/260#pullrequestreview-5596694933).
3. **Pre-inverse CCF DC conditioning exposes a shared numerical weakness.** Conditioning both implementations yields 0/60 large-disagreement screen positives and very small native trajectory differences in the nonfailure cases, while conditioning CPU alone changes some CPU products substantially. This is evidence against treating the unconditioned CPU result as ground truth. It is still agreement/stability evidence, not absolute accuracy.
4. **Shared failure survives excellent agreement.** In the conditioned e10216-01 case, both paths exhaust five global iterations with final incremental RMSD about 58.57 px, yet produce closely agreeing images and exit 0. That must remain a separate nonconvergence/quality result, not disappear in a 0/60 headline. [Attribution review](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/pull/261#pullrequestreview-5596698867).

### Acceptance hierarchy

The existing `docs/gate_contract.md` already separates CPU regression, backend diagnostics, motion truth and scientific outcome. Apply it consistently:

**Specified operation + independent numerical oracle → known-motion and property tests → held-out scientific outcomes.** Backend/legacy differences explain changes and detect unexpected regressions; they cannot decide which implementation is physically correct. A reference calculation may run on a CPU without making the production CPU pipeline its oracle.

Do not replace the old relative-RMSE cutoff with a looser arbitrary cutoff. Preserve old profiles/results, and explicitly version the contract and fixtures for intentional algorithm/correctness changes. The 0.1 S1 screen is not a release gate; the named backend profile's 0.001 relative-RMSE diagnostic is itself nonblocking, while its other checks still apply.

### Ordered work, reusing the existing owners

**A. Finish the two narrow repairs.** Complete #254's independently projected/analytic valid-spectrum output reference and signal-preservation controls, retaining the new five-site invariant mutants. Qualify #260 against independently known parabola vertices/high-precision same-sample evaluation. Keep native guard/edge/nonfinite and unchanged-path controls. Measure actual cost rather than assume selective FP64/projection is free. Neither change needs the entire science campaign to justify its local mathematical defect; their combined scientific support remains separately qualified.

**B. Make #262 the next bounded numerical experiment.** With Hermitian repair and the scalar fit fixed, independently vary global-CCF and local-CCF DC removal: neither, global only, local only, both. Zero only the CCF spectrum's DC bin before inverse, not resident movie or published-image DC. Use analytic/high-precision CCFs and stage-level offset/contrast tests before rerunning real movies. Preserve estimator/tie/acceptance choices initially. [Detailed independent-oracle and truth-test brief](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/issues/262#issuecomment-6311268237).

**C. Expand motion-truth qualification rather than another parity-only census.** Reuse `generate_known_motion_fixture.py` and the existing field checker. Its continuous analytic Gaussian synthesis is a good starting point; the current local field lies inside the fitted model and the noisy accuracy case still fails as characterization. Add independent noise seeds, realistic weak signal, pedestal/contrast sweeps, abrupt motion, large/nonsquare geometries and declared grouping/binning cases. Test in-model recovery separately from out-of-model robustness. Measure vector field error in pixels/Å, tails and temporal errors, true-signal retention, boundary effects, ambiguity and failure rates. Do not generate every fixture with the same production Fourier/interpolation helper under test. Capture full-precision runtime models separately from serialized models.

**D. Treat global nonconvergence and unsupported peaks as first-class quality states.** Trace the e10216-01 return/publication path and define how nonconvergence or unidentifiable motion is communicated, rejected or retried. An exit-0 product is not sufficient evidence of an estimated trajectory. Test healthy controls plus nonconverged, no-signal and boundary-maximum cases, including batch/aggregate status. Choose a recovery/refusal policy explicitly; do not indiscriminately increase iterations or clamp peaks until legacy agreement improves. #263's boundary policy and #264's actual-domain guard are separate focused work, with prospective truth/validity tests.

**E. Prepare and run S1.4 on a frozen candidate without waiting for zero CPU discrepancy.** Use #61's prospective protocol: held-out collections, matched particles/half-set assignments/masks/downstream settings for a controlled comparison, CTF as an initial screen and independent half-map FSC/relative B-factor as complementary outcomes. Evaluate before downstream motion re-estimation can erase differences, then evaluate the normal complete workflow separately. Set scientific non-inferiority margins before inspecting held-out outcomes, and estimate uncertainty by movie/collection, not pixels or repeated grids. Keep the present 30-movie census as development evidence, not the only validation population.

**F. Integrate and audit the actual combined build.** Preserve input/metadata/failure invariants, source/binary/device/route provenance, old failed records and the union of required tests. Test the combined Release CPU/CUDA/nvCOMP build and representative formerly negative families. Controlled whole-movie performance is separate from shared-host correctness runs.

### Independent correctness queue

#258 gain semantics, #259 source-boundary interpolation, #264 guard coordinates, #265 coefficient round-trip and #266 CPU C2R input validity should be assessed against explicit mathematical/data contracts. Inherited provenance is important for compatibility notes, but not a scientific reason to preserve a defect. Conversely, being inherited does not prove every repair must change products; measure the actual changes. For #265 use real pre-write native coefficients, not a fit reconstructed from already-rounded STAR observations. For #266 separate valid-input projection from the broader fractional-Nyquist/crop-folding policy.

**Current stopping point:** mathematical repairs substantially supported; shared DC conditioning strongly motivated; low-SNR accuracy, shared nonconvergence policy, broader held-out scientific outcomes and production cost are not yet established. No merge, production edit, new GPU job or closure is made by this plan.

title: S1: CPU vs CUDA local alignment divergence — post-RC0 campaign (S1.1–S1.4)
